issue.title: Message board: athena agent completion supervision, epoch 016 (2026-09-07)
issue.description:
Purpose and authorization
This memory task bead is an operational message board for Bryan's explicitly requested
sequence of SASE agents that supervise every agent running on athena until each one
completes its assigned work. It is a proof of concept for whether a dedicated
message-board bead type would be useful; record evidence bearing on that question as
you go. No memory-file edit and no new bead-type implementation is requested.
Append-only attributed notes are the baton between successors. Keep this bead open
(never ready) so it raises no Memory TaskTriage gate; that lifecycle intentionally does
not apply to this operational log.

Epoch lineage
This board roots supervision epoch 016 (setup agent 016, model claude-fable-5,
launched by Bryan ~2026-09-07T01:48Z). Predecessors: bead:sase-xs (epoch 00a) and
bead:sase-xt (epoch 00b). The 00b chain died mechanically: its check-in agent 00b--1
attempted mid-turn retry launches that raised LaunchApproval gate
launch-19a075c1-4f41-4126-8380-41e9f1ddf9a2 ("1 slot"); creating the gate ended its
turn before any hourly monitor was scheduled, and Bryan REJECTED the gate at
2026-09-07T01:44Z, then launched this new epoch. Retain and reconcile prior-board
evidence; never close, edit, or overwrite the older boards. This board is the current
baton. If an older supervisor somehow reappears, reconcile ownership through board
notes before acting on the same failed run.

Model policy
Every agent in this chain between the first and the last uses codex/gpt-6-astra
(supervisors at xhigh: codex/gpt-6-astra@xhigh). Only the setup agent (016) and the
final analysis agent use claude-fable-5. Monitors MUST pass -m codex/gpt-6-astra@xhigh
explicitly alongside --next: never omit -m, because this family's root model is
claude-fable-5 and an omitted -m inherits the starter's model. Retries/restarts of
supervised agents preserve their original task but are explicitly routed to
codex/gpt-6-astra; healthy already-running agents keep their existing settings.

Launch policy (CRITICAL)
Never use the /sase_run skill and never ask Bryan for permission before launching
agents. Bryan pre-authorized every launch this chain needs: investigation, repairs,
commits via /sase_git_commit, retries, restarts, and monitor successors. SASE agent
launches triggered after sase monitors complete need no approval. Use the installed
`sase agent restart NAME` (preview with --dry-run first because it can delete related
artifacts and old evidence, then --yes) and `sase run '<safely quoted prompt>'`
directly. Known hazard, cause of epoch 00b's death: a mid-turn `sase run` can raise a
LaunchApproval gate under runner-slot contention, and creating a gate ends your turn
mechanically, so no hourly monitor gets scheduled and the chain dies. Mitigations, in
order: (a) check runner capacity and queue state before any mid-turn launch; (b) when
contention is plausible, embed the launch in your next monitor's command instead, e.g.
`sase monitor start ... -m codex/gpt-6-astra@xhigh -n '<next check-in prompt>' --
sh -c 'sase run <quoted prompt>; sleep 3600'`, so the launch happens outside any agent
turn and the chain survives either way — but record the intended launch on this board
BEFORE starting that monitor. If an installed command itself refuses, record the
precise refusal, pursue supported recovery, and keep supervision alive rather than
declaring success. Do not invent approvals for unrelated human decisions or bypass an
actual security control.

Ordered check-in procedure
1. Read this description, the latest checkpoint note, and every unresolved ledger
   item. Capture fresh `sase agent list -a -j` (machine-wide; completed rows capped at
   50 per project) and `sase monitor list -a --json`; use uncapped
   `sase agent search 'status:FAILED' -j -l 0` so caps or row disappearance cannot
   hide failures; check `sase gate list`. Compare per-run keys (project, name,
   started_at, PID, artifacts_dir) and progress fingerprints (file sizes/mtimes,
   done.json) against the prior checkpoint. A long runtime, a quiet planning shell, or
   an old plan row sharing a PID with a live code row is NOT a stall; stable done.json
   is authoritative after exit while live_reply.md is draft. For confirmed stalls: fix
   the underlying cause when appropriate, verify, commit fixes with /sase_git_commit,
   then relaunch unfinished/uncommitted work (`sase agent restart`, dry-run first).
2. Investigate every new or still-unresolved FAILED assignment. Search for already-live
   or successful replacements before launching another. For an ordinary failed retry,
   recover the IDENTICAL stored raw_xprompt.md task, changing only identity and model:
   use allocate_retry_name from sase.agent.names, rewrite_retry_prompt_name from
   sase.agent.relaunch_prompt (clan/family aware), and set_prompt_model from
   sase.xprompt.directive_edit; the explicit %id must place the new run in the failed
   agent's hood (e.g. failed-name.r0). Preserve project/VCS routing, bead linkage,
   dependencies, workflows, and finalizers. Never replace the raw task with a
   paraphrase and never silently reroute a GitHub task to home. Record intent BEFORE
   launching and outcome AFTER; a live retry is pending recovery, not a resolved
   failure. Avoid duplicate active retries and blind retry loops; persistent transient
   failures wait for the next hourly cycle.
3. Reconcile the durable ledger, then take a fresh inventory. Termination requires:
   zero running/waiting/queued target agents, zero active dependent monitors or
   pending continuations, and zero failed assignments without verified successful
   recovery — excluding only this supervision family (016 and its own sleep monitors).
   Gates awaiting Bryan's own decision (e.g. a plan approval) are HIS to answer: track
   them prominently, never answer them for him, and do not treat an otherwise-finished
   machine as unfinished solely because such a user-owned gate is pending — record it
   in the final analysis instead. Confirm termination with a second fresh inventory
   after reconciliation. If not met: append your checkpoint note, then as your LAST
   action run
   `sase monitor start -s SLEEPING -S SLEPT -t 70m -L 'Agent supervision'
   -r 'Hourly completion check; board <this bead ID>' -m codex/gpt-6-astra@xhigh
   --next-output none -n '<self-contained successor prompt carrying this bead ID,
   cycle number, launch policy, and model policy>' -- sleep 3600`.
   A successful monitor start ends your turn mechanically; a NONZERO exit is NOT a
   handoff — diagnose and retry it. The installed CLI takes the command after `--`
   (there is no --command flag); timeout must exceed the sleep; no idle timeout for a
   deliberate quiet sleep.
4. If termination is proven, use the /sase_pipe skill to hand off to a final agent on
   model claude-fable-5 whose prompt instructs it to: verify the termination evidence
   itself, then leave a concise analysis — interventions performed, commits/tests,
   retry outcomes, timestamped zero-target evidence, why the termination condition is
   definitely met, and observations on this message-board experiment — BOTH as a note
   on this bead AND as its normal final reply. It must not schedule another monitor.

Checkpoint format
Open with UTC timestamp, supervisor agent name, predecessor, and cycle number. Then:
compact running/waiting/queued list with per-run keys; unresolved failed-run→retry
mapping; progress evidence; interventions with commit/test receipts; newly verified
completions; remaining actions; termination decision; next sleep duration. Save bulky
inventories as indexed artifacts (`sase artifact create`, after reading the
sase_artifacts memory) and link canonical refs instead of embedding megabytes; read
them back only with `sase artifact read <ref> "<reason>"`. Append with
`sase bead note <this bead ID> "<text>"`; never edit or remove predecessors' notes.

Boundaries
/sase_repo before reading or editing any checkout other than your own workspace;
shared backend behavior belongs in sase-core. Read the lint_and_test memory before
finishing any change to the sase repo; verification is not optional. /sase_git_commit
is authorized only for actual repairs; no empty commits for observation. Out-of-scope
discoveries go through /sase_new_task (supervisors may create task beads). Never
hand-edit bead statuses that the runtime owns.

Metadata
Owner: Bryan. Host: athena. Epoch root: 016. Chain model: codex/gpt-6-astra@xhigh.
Size: large is planning metadata (unknown cross-project repair scope), not a request to
launch a task worker. Required memory-type fields below are honest sentinels; evaluate
the message-board experiment without filing a feature task merely to propose a new
bead type.
